words.en: Violence is behavior which is intended to hurt, injure, or kill people.

words.ex: The weather today is dreadful.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气令人不快。
words.en: If you say that something is dreadful, you mean that it is very bad or unpleasant, or very poor in quality.

words.ex: The movie was incredible.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影太棒了。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as incredible, you like them very much or are impressed by them, because they are extremely or unusually good.

words.ex: He rolled up his sleeve to wash his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他卷起袖子洗手。
words.en: The part of a garment that covers the arm.

words.tr: v. 调整；使适合；使适应；
words.ex: He adjusted the chair to sit comfortably.
words.ex_cn: 他调整了椅子以便坐得舒服。
words.en: To adjust something means to change it so that it is more effective or appropriate, or so that it fits better.

words.ex: The paint was applied unevenly on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 油漆在墙上涂得不均匀。
words.en: In a way that is not level, smooth, or regular.

words.ex: It was an utter mistake.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个完全的错误。
words.en: To say something or to make a sound with your voice; complete or absolute.

words.tr:
n. 蔑视
v. 蔑视
words.ex: He looked at the lie with scorn.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看着这个谎言。
words.en: If you scorn someone or something, you feel or show contempt for them.

words.ex: She walked nakedly into the room.
words.ex_cn: 她裸体走进房间。
words.en: In a way that is not hidden or disguised; openly.

words.tr:
v. 跛行；蹒跚；瘸着走
adj. 无力的；无生气的
words.ex: He limps after hurting his leg.
words.ex_cn: 他受伤后走路一瘸一拐。
words.en: If someone limps, they walk with difficulty or in an uneven way because one of their legs or feet is hurt.

words.ex: Her self-consciousness made it hard for her to speak in front of a crowd.
words.ex_cn: 她的害羞使她在人群前讲话变得困难。
words.en: Self-consciousness is the feeling of being aware of oneself as an individual or of one's own being, actions, or thoughts.

words.tr:
v. 弯腰；俯身；卑屈；俯冲
n. 弯腰；屈背；屈服；俯冲
words.ex: He must stoop to enter the small door.
words.ex_cn: 他必须弯腰才能进入那扇小门。
words.en: If someone stoops, they bend their body forwards and downwards.

words.tr:
n. 圣歌；赞美诗；喊叫
v. 吟唱；诵扬；反复叫喊
words.ex: The monks sang a traditional chant during the morning prayer.
words.ex_cn: 修道士们在晨祷时唱了一首传统圣歌。
words.en: A chant is a word or group of words that is repeated over and over again. It can also refer to a simple song, especially one that is sung in a religious service.

words.ex: He kept his dignity even when he was poor.
words.ex_cn: 即使他很穷，他依然保持尊严。
words.en: Dignity is the quality of being worthy of honor or respect.

words.ex: The judge will summon him tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 法官明天将传唤他。
words.en: If you summon someone, you order them to come to you.

words.ex: The beach has sandy soil.
words.ex_cn: 这个海滩有含沙的土壤。
words.en: Covered with or consisting mostly of sand.

words.ex: He perspires heavily when he runs.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步时大量出汗。
words.en: To perspire means to produce liquid through your skin because you are hot or frightened.

words.tr:
v. 咕哝地抱怨；嘀咕
n. 咕哝地抱怨；嘀咕
words.ex: He mutters under his breath when he is angry.
words.ex_cn: 当他生气时，他会低声嘟囔。
words.en: To speak or say something in a low voice that is hard to hear, often because you are annoyed or complaining.

words.ex: The cake has three layers of chocolate.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕有三层巧克力。
words.en: A layer of a substance or material is a quantity or piece of it that covers a surface or that is between two other things.

words.ex: The heat was inescapable in the small room.
words.ex_cn: 小房间里热得无法逃避。
words.en: If you describe a fact, situation, or activity as inescapable, you mean that it is difficult not to notice it or be affected by it.

words.ex: The accident was a serious incident.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是一起严重事件。
words.en: An incident is an event that is either unpleasant or unusual.

words.ex: He is on his way to school.
words.ex_cn: 他正在去学校的路上。
words.en: If you are on your way to a place, you are traveling towards it and have not yet arrived.

words.tr: adj. 悲惨的；不幸的；难过的；恶劣的
words.ex: He felt wretched after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到很悲惨。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as wretched, you mean that they are in a very bad or unfortunate situation.

words.tr: phrase. 出错； 发生故障；误入歧途
words.ex: Things can go wrong if you don't follow the instructions.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不按照说明做，事情可能会出错。
words.en: If a situation or event goes wrong, it does not happen in the way you intended or expected, and often has a bad result.

words.tr:
v. 陷入（困境）；设圈套；
n. 圈套；陷阱；困境；
words.ex: He trapped himself in debt by spending too much.
words.ex_cn: 他因花钱太多而陷入债务困境。
words.en: A trap is a device or enclosure designed to catch and retain animals, typically by allowing entry but not exit or by catching hold of a part of the body.

words.tr: phrase. 停止运转；出故障；分解；感情失控
words.ex: The machine broke down yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器昨天坏了。
words.en: If a machine or vehicle breaks down, it stops working. If a discussion, relationship, or system breaks down, it fails because of a problem or disagreement.

words.ex: He is irritable when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 他累了的时候容易烦躁。
words.en: If someone is irritable, they are easily annoyed.

words.tr: phrase. 办理入住手续；调查，查证
words.ex: He will check into the hotel in the evening.
words.ex_cn: 他将在晚上办理酒店入住。
words.en: To register one's arrival at a hotel, airport, etc., or to investigate something.

words.tr: adj. 破旧的；肮脏破烂的；衣衫褴褛的
words.ex: He wore a shabby coat to school.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着一件破旧的外套去学校。
words.en: If you describe something as shabby, you mean that it looks old and is in poor condition.

words.tr:
adj. 联合的；共同的；
n. 关节；接合处；
words.ex: They signed a joint agreement to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一项联合协议来保护环境。
words.en: A joint is a place where two things are joined together, especially the place where two bones are connected in a person's or animal's body.

words.ex: We decorate the room for the party.
words.ex_cn: 我们为派对装饰房间。
words.en: To make something look more attractive by putting things on it or around it.

words.ex: The greasy pan needed a good wash.
words.ex_cn: 这个油污的平底锅需要好好洗一洗。
words.en: Something that is greasy has a lot of grease or oil on it or in it.

words.ex: The cat occupies the sofa all day.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫整天占据着沙发。
words.en: If people or things occupy a place, they are in it or fill it.

words.ex: He did the homework by himself.
words.ex_cn: 他独自完成了作业。
words.en: Without help from anyone else; alone.

words.ex: He did the homework all by himself.
words.ex_cn: 他完全独自完成了作业。
words.en: Without any help from anyone else; completely alone.

words.ex: He spoke monotonously during the lecture.
words.ex_cn: 他在讲座中单调地说话。
words.en: In a manner that lacks variety and interest; tediously uniform or repetitive.

words.ex: He felt miserable after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到很悲惨。
words.en: If you are miserable, you are very unhappy.

words.ex: My mom scolded me for coming home late.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈因为我回家晚而责备了我。
words.en: If you scold someone, you speak angrily to them because they have done something wrong.

words.ex: The soldiers defend their country from enemies.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们保卫自己的国家免受敌人入侵。
words.en: To defend means to protect someone or something from attack, harm, or criticism. It can also involve arguing in support of someone or something.

words.tr:
v. 拍；掴；拍击
n. 拍；掴；拍击
words.ex: He slapped the table in anger.
words.ex_cn: 他生气地拍了桌子。
words.en: If you slap someone, you hit them with the palm of your hand.

words.tr:
adj. 次要的；轻微的；小的；小调的；
n. 未成年人；
words.ex: The mistake was a minor error.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误是一个小错误。
words.en: A minor is a person who is under the age at which they legally become an adult.

words.ex: He interrupted me while I was speaking.
words.ex_cn: 我在说话时他打断了我。
words.en: To interrupt someone means to stop them from speaking by saying or doing something, or to cause something to stop happening for a period of time.

words.tr: n. 一阵强劲的气流；爆炸；
words.ex: A blast of cold wind hit the window.
words.ex_cn: 一阵冷风击中了窗户。
words.en: A blast is a sudden loud noise or a strong gust of wind. It can also refer to an explosion or the act of blowing something up. As a verb, it means to explode or to criticize severely.

words.tr:
n. 滴落；油滴
v. 滴落；“drip”的现在分词
adj. 湿淋淋的
words.ex: The dripping from the faucet woke me up.
words.ex_cn: 水龙头的滴落声把我吵醒了。
words.en: The act or sound of liquid falling in drops.

words.ex: He wore a ragged coat in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天穿着一件破旧的外套。
words.en: Clothes that are ragged are old and torn.

words.tr:
adj. 破旧的；精疲力尽的；耗尽的
n. 扼要报告；描述细节；详细情况；缩减
words.ex: The old house is run-down and needs repair.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子破旧不堪，需要维修。
words.en: In poor physical condition; tired and weak.

words.ex: Monsieur Dupont is a distinguished guest.
words.ex_cn: 杜邦先生是一位尊贵的客人。
words.en: A title or form of address for a man, especially a Frenchman, corresponding to Mr. or sir.

words.tr: adv. 疲惫地；厌倦地；百无聊赖地
words.ex: He walked wearily up the stairs after a long day at work.
words.ex_cn: 在工作了一整天后，他疲倦地走上楼梯。
words.en: In a manner showing tiredness, especially as a result of excessive exertion or lack of sleep.

words.ex: He spoke hoarsely after a long day of shouting.
words.ex_cn: 经过一天的喊叫，他说话变得嘶哑。
words.en: In a rough or harsh voice, often as a result of a sore throat or shouting.

words.ex: The tip of the pencil broke off.
words.ex_cn: 铅笔的尖端断了。
words.en: The end of a pointed or projecting object; a sum of money given to someone as a reward for their services; to give someone a small amount of money as a reward for their services.

words.tr:
n. 新闻界；出版社；
v. 按；压；
words.ex: The press reported the news quickly.
words.ex_cn: 新闻界迅速报道了这则新闻。
words.en: To press something is to push it firmly, often with your fingers or hand, in order to operate a device or machine, or to make something flat or smooth. It can also mean to urge someone to do something or to make a strong demand for something.

words.tr:
adj. 精瘦的；精简的；不景气的；
v. 倾斜；倚靠；
words.ex: The dog is lean and fast.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗精瘦而敏捷。
words.en: If you lean in a particular direction, you bend your body in that direction. If you lean on or against someone or something, you rest against them so that they partly support your weight. If you describe someone as lean, you mean that they are thin but look strong and healthy. If you describe a period of time as lean, you mean that it is a time when people have very little of something, especially money.

words.ex: The ancient Egyptians built the pyramids.
words.ex_cn: 古埃及人建造了金字塔。
words.en: Belonging to the very distant past and no longer in existence.

words.tr: v. （使）变直；（使）变平；（使）变整齐；
words.ex: He straightened the crooked picture on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 他把墙上歪斜的画扶直了。
words.en: To make something straight or to put something in order.

words.tr: phrase. 挺直身体；整理；收拾整齐；改过自新
words.ex: He straightened up when the teacher entered the room.
words.ex_cn: 老师进房间时，他挺直了身体。
words.en: To make something tidy or to improve one's behavior or posture.

words.ex: He asked for permission to leave early.
words.ex_cn: 他请求允许早点离开。
words.en: If someone who has authority over you gives you permission to do something, they say that they will allow you to do it.

words.ex: The motion of the ball is very fast.
words.ex_cn: 球的运动非常快。
words.en: The action or process of moving or being moved.

words.ex: The children are merry on Christmas day.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在圣诞节那天很开心。
words.en: If you describe someone's character or behavior as merry, you mean that they are happy and cheerful.

words.ex: He will depart tomorrow morning.
words.ex_cn: 他明天早上离开。
words.en: If you depart from a place, you leave it and start a journey to another place.

words.ex: The bomb will explode at noon.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹将在中午爆炸。
words.en: If an object explodes, it bursts loudly and with great force, often causing damage or injury.

words.tr:
n. 炸弹
v. 投弹于；轰炸
words.ex: The bomb exploded at noon.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹在中午爆炸了。
words.en: A bomb is a device which explodes and damages or destroys a large area.

words.tr: v. 跛行；蹒跚；捆绑（马等的）两腿
words.ex: The old man hobbled along the street.
words.ex_cn: 那位老人一瘸一拐地走在街上。
words.en: If you hobble, you walk in an awkward way, usually because your feet or legs hurt.

words.tr:
n. 人们；人民；
adj. 民间的；
words.ex: The folk in the village are very friendly.
words.ex_cn: 村子里的人们非常友好。
words.en: Folk can refer to people in general, or to a particular group of people. It can also refer to traditional music or customs of a community.

words.ex: They had a feast on New Year's Day.
words.ex_cn: 他们在元旦举办了一场盛宴。
words.en: A feast is a large and special meal, often to celebrate something.

words.tr:
n. 魔术；魔法；
adj. 魔术（似）的；神奇的；
words.ex: He performed magic at the birthday party.
words.ex_cn: 他在生日聚会上表演了魔术。
words.en: Magic is the power to use supernatural forces to make impossible things happen, such as making people disappear or controlling events in nature.

words.ex: He arrived in time for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他赶上了公交车。
words.en: If you say that something will happen in time or given time, you mean that it will happen eventually, after a lot of time has passed.

words.tr: adj. 发光的；辐射的；容光焕发的
words.ex: The radiant sun warmed the garden.
words.ex_cn: 明亮的太阳温暖了花园。
words.en: If you describe someone as radiant, you mean that they look very happy and healthy.

words.ex: The children's laughter filled the room.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们的笑声充满了房间。
words.en: The sound of people laughing, especially when it is loud and continuous.

words.tr:
v. 怒吼；吼叫；咆哮
n. 咆哮；怒号
words.ex: The bull bellowed loudly in the field.
words.ex_cn: 公牛在田野里大声吼叫。
words.en: If someone bellows, they shout angrily in a loud, deep voice.

words.tr: adj. 不受约束的；无拘无束的
words.ex: He sang uninhibited at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上毫无拘束地唱歌。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as uninhibited, you mean that they express their opinions and feelings openly, and behave as they want to, without worrying what other people think.

words.ex: He showed great enthusiasm for learning English.
words.ex_cn: 他对学习英语表现出极大的热情。
words.en: Enthusiasm is a strong feeling of excitement and interest in something and a desire to become involved in it.

words.ex: The doctor checked his gut for signs of infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他的肠道是否有感染迹象。
words.en: The gut refers to the stomach and other internal organs of an animal or person, often used to describe the digestive tract. It can also metaphorically represent courage or determination.

words.ex: He finally embraced the new idea.
words.ex_cn: 他最终接受了这个新想法。
words.en: To take someone into your arms as a sign of love or affection, or to accept something enthusiastically.

words.ex: The lad is playing soccer with his friends.
words.ex_cn: 那个男孩正在和朋友们踢足球。
words.en: A lad is a young man or boy.

words.tr: v. 兑现；递送；交付；发表；为…接生；
words.ex: He promised to deliver on his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他承诺要兑现自己的目标。
words.en: To bring and hand over (a letter, parcel, or ordered goods) to the proper recipient or address.

words.ex: They drank champagne at the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他们在婚礼上喝了香槟。
words.en: Champagne is an expensive French white wine with bubbles in. It is often drunk to celebrate something.

words.tr:
prep. 在…周围；环绕；
adv. 环绕；附近；
adj. 圆的；十足的；
n. 回合；圆形物；
v. 拐过；使成圆形；
words.ex: The children sat round the fire.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们围坐在火堆旁。
words.en: Something that is round is shaped like a circle or a ball.

words.tr: n. 诺埃尔（姓氏）；圣诞节
words.ex: The church bells rang out the Noel.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的钟声敲响了圣诞节的到来。
words.en: Noel is a term used to refer to Christmas or Christmas carols, often used in songs and poems to evoke the spirit of the holiday season.

words.tr: phrase. 保持节拍；计时；守时；准确地计时
words.ex: The old clock cannot keep time well.
words.ex_cn: 这个旧钟不能很好地保持准确时间。
words.en: To keep time is to maintain a regular rhythm or pace, especially in music or in measuring time.

words.tr: n. 颂歌；赞美诗；欢乐之歌；
words.ex: The children sang a Christmas carol at the party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在派对上唱了一首圣诞颂歌。
words.en: A carol is a religious song or popular hymn, particularly one associated with Christmas.

words.tr:
n. 释放；发布；
v. 释放；发布；
words.ex: The release of the prisoner made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯的释放让每个人都高兴。
words.en: To release something means to let it go or to allow it to be free, or to make something available to the public.

words.tr: v. 厚厚地覆盖；使…窒息；闷死
words.ex: He tried to smother the fire with a blanket.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用毯子把火闷灭。
words.en: To smother someone or something means to kill them by covering their face so that they cannot breathe, or to put out a fire by covering it.

words.ex: He spends hours in cyberspace every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天在虚拟空间里花几个小时。
words.en: Cyberspace is the notional environment in which communication over computer networks occurs.

words.ex: He is a novice at playing the guitar.
words.ex_cn: 他是个吉他新手。
words.en: A novice is someone who has just started learning or doing something and does not have much experience.

words.ex: It's a paradox that he is rich but unhappy.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个悖论，他很富有却不快乐。
words.en: A paradox is a statement that seems to contradict itself but may nonetheless be true, or a situation that defies intuition.

words.tr: v. 告诉；讲述；“tell”的现在分词； adj. 有力的；反映情况的；
words.ex: He told me the news.
words.ex_cn: 他告诉了我这个消息。
words.en: If something is telling, it shows the true nature of a situation or someone's feelings or character in a very clear way.

words.tr:
n. 大楼；大厦；块；街区；障碍物；
v. 阻塞；阻碍；
words.ex: The new block is next to the park.
words.ex_cn: 这栋新大楼就在公园旁边。
words.en: A block is a large solid piece of material with flat surfaces on each side. As a verb, to block means to prevent movement or progress.

words.ex: My colleague helped me with the report.
words.ex_cn: 我的同事帮我完成了报告。
words.en: A colleague is someone you work with, especially in a professional job.

words.ex: He is a maven in the field of computer science.
words.ex_cn: 他是计算机科学领域的专家。
words.en: A maven is someone who is very knowledgeable about a particular subject.

words.ex: He felt hunger after running for an hour.
words.ex_cn: 他跑了一个小时后感到饥饿。
words.en: A strong desire or need for food.

words.ex: He still hungers after knowledge, even at the age of seventy.
words.ex_cn: 即使到了七十岁，他仍然渴望知识。
words.en: To have a strong desire or craving for something.

words.tr: phrase. 紧紧握住；坚持下去；保留
words.ex: He hangs on to his old wallet because it reminds him of his dad.
words.ex_cn: 他紧紧保留着旧钱包，因为它让他想起爸爸。
words.en: To keep something that you have, especially because it might be useful or valuable in the future.

words.ex: The movie was far too long for my taste.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影对我来说太长了。
words.en: Far too is used to emphasize that something is more than is desirable, necessary, or acceptable.

words.ex: He gave up smoking last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年戒烟了。
words.en: If you give up something, you stop doing it or having it.

words.ex: He used to play soccer every day.
words.ex_cn: 他过去每天踢足球。
words.en: If something used to be done or used to be the case, it was done regularly in the past or was the case in the past.

words.ex: He resents being ignored by his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他怨恨被老板忽视。
words.en: If you resent someone or something, you feel bitter and angry about them.

words.ex: He will install the new software on his computer.
words.ex_cn: 他将在他的电脑上安装新软件。
words.en: To set up or fix in position for use or service.

words.tr: phrase. 赠送；分发；背叛；泄露
words.ex: He will give away his old books to the library.
words.ex_cn: 他将把他的旧书捐给图书馆。
words.en: To give something to someone without asking for payment, or to reveal something secret or private.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 赠送某物；泄露秘密；无意中透露信息
words.ex: He gave his old toys away to poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他把旧玩具送给了穷孩子。
words.en: To reveal a secret or give something for free.

words.ex: He is hooked on video games.
words.ex_cn: 他沉迷于电子游戏。
words.en: If you are hooked on something, you enjoy it so much that it takes up a lot of your interest and attention.

words.tr: phrase. 上瘾的；着迷的；被迷住的
words.ex: I was hooked on the show after watching the first episode.
words.ex_cn: 看了第一集之后，我就被这部剧吸引住了。
words.en: To be very interested in or very involved with something, often to the point of addiction.

words.ex: He got hooked on the TV show after watching one episode.
words.ex_cn: 他看完一集电视剧后就上瘾了。
words.en: To become addicted or very interested in something.

words.tr: phrase. 对某事上瘾的；沉迷于某事的
words.ex: She has been hooked on online games for years.
words.ex_cn: 她对网络游戏上瘾已经好几年了。
words.en: To be very interested in or enthusiastic about something, often to the point of addiction.

words.tr:
v. 提升；提高；改进；
n. 增加；改进；
words.ex: He upgraded his phone to get better performance.
words.ex_cn: 他升级了手机以获得更好的性能。
words.en: To upgrade means to improve the quality or usefulness of something, or to raise it to a higher standard. It can also refer to the process of improving or raising something.

words.ex: He drove a souped-up sports car.
words.ex_cn: 他驾驶着一辆经过改装的跑车。
words.en: Modified or enhanced to perform better or have more power, especially in reference to vehicles or engines.

words.tr: adj. 延长的；扩大范围的；延伸的；
words.ex: The meeting was extended by thirty minutes.
words.ex_cn: 会议被延长了三十分钟。
words.en: Made larger or longer than usual.

words.ex: They talked face to face instead of on the phone.
words.ex_cn: 他们面对面交谈，而不是打电话。
words.en: If you meet or talk to someone face to face, you meet or talk to them directly, rather than by telephone, email, or online.

words.tr: phrase. 面对面地；直接面对（某人或某种情况）
words.ex: He is face to face with his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他正面对面地和他的老师说话。
words.en: In a situation where you are directly confronting or dealing with someone or something.

words.ex: He barely slept last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚几乎没睡觉。
words.en: You use barely to say that something is only just true or only just the case.

words.tr: phrase. 倾诉衷肠；敞开心扉；尽情吐露心声
words.ex: He sat with his friend and poured out his heart.
words.ex_cn: 他和朋友坐着，倾诉了内心。
words.en: To express one's feelings or thoughts openly and emotionally to someone else.

words.tr: phrase. 倾诉衷肠；毫无保留地倾诉心事；敞开心扉
words.ex: He poured his heart out to his best friend during the walk.
words.ex_cn: 他在散步时向他最好的朋友倾诉了心声。
words.en: To express one's feelings or thoughts in a very open and emotional way.

words.tr: phrase. 畅所欲言；打开；开放
words.ex: Please open up and tell me how you really feel.
words.ex_cn: 请畅所欲言，告诉我你真正的感受。
words.en: To make something available or accessible; to start or begin something.

words.tr: phrase. 用电话交谈；在通话
words.ex: He is talking on the phone with his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他正在和妈妈打电话。
words.en: Using the telephone to communicate with someone.

words.ex: The architect had to consider the obliqueness of the roof when designing the building.
words.ex_cn: 建筑师在设计建筑物时必须考虑屋顶的斜度。
words.en: The quality or state of being oblique; deviation from a straight line or course; indirectness.

words.tr: phrase. 零碎的东西；少量而分散的（尤指金钱或资源）
words.ex: He paid his debt in dribs and drabs.
words.ex_cn: 他一点一点地还清了债务。
words.en: If something happens or is given out in dribs and drabs, it happens or is given out in small amounts over a period of time, rather than all at once.

words.tr: phrase. 零零星星地；一点一点地；断断续续地
words.ex: He pays his debt in dribs and drabs.
words.ex_cn: 他一点一点地还债。
words.en: In small, irregular amounts or pieces over a period of time.

words.ex: He felt intense pain after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他感到剧烈的疼痛。
words.en: If you describe an activity as intense, you mean that it is very serious and concentrated, and often involves doing a great deal in a short time.

words.tr: adj. 压迫的；压力下的；逼近的
words.ex: She felt a bearing-down pain during labor.
words.ex_cn: 她在分娩时感到一种下压般的疼痛。
words.en: The act of applying pressure or effort, especially in childbirth or a difficult task.

words.tr: 短语动词. 占上风；取得优势
words.ex: By studying the opponent's strategies, they managed to get the upper hand in the negotiations.
words.ex_cn: 通过研究对手的策略，他们在谈判中获得了优势。
words.en: To gain a position of advantage or control over someone or something.

words.ex: Children tend to be more active in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 孩子往往在早上更活跃。
words.en: If someone tends to do something, they usually do it or they often do it.

words.ex: He tends to arrive late for class.
words.ex_cn: 他总是迟到上课。
words.en: If someone or something tends to do a particular thing, they usually do it or they often do it.

words.ex: He tends towards quietness when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，他倾向于变得安静。
words.en: To have a tendency or inclination to move in a particular direction or to be attracted to a particular idea or way of thinking.

words.tr:
n. 辩论；讨论；
v. 辩论；讨论；
words.ex: The students had a debate about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学生们就作业进行了一场辩论。
words.en: If you maintain something, you continue to have it, and do not let it stop or grow weaker.

words.ex: The two companies showed good cooperation on the project.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司在这个项目上表现出良好的合作。
words.en: Cooperation is the process of working or acting together, which can be seen in many aspects of life, including business, science, and social interactions.

words.ex: The magic show captivates the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If you are captivated by someone or something, you find them fascinating and attractive.

words.ex: She typically arrives early for class.
words.ex_cn: 她往往很早就到课。
words.en: You use typically to say that something usually happens in the way that you are describing.

words.tr:
n. 结构；建筑物；
v. 组织；
words.ex: The structure of the bridge is very strong.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥的结构非常坚固。
words.en: The arrangement of and relations between the parts or elements of something complex.

words.ex: He dominates the conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他主宰了谈话。
words.en: To dominate means to control or govern someone or something, or to be the most important or noticeable feature of something.

words.tr:
v. 畏缩不前；犹豫；妨碍
n. 阻碍，妨碍
words.ex: He balks at paying high prices.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意支付高价。
words.en: If you balk at something, you hesitate to do it or agree to it, often because it is unpleasant or difficult.

words.tr: adj. 适当的；合适的；恰当的；
words.ex: This dress is appropriate for a wedding.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子适合参加婚礼。
words.en: Something that is appropriate is suitable or acceptable for a particular situation.

words.ex: He tried to incite a riot with his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过演讲煽动暴乱。
words.en: To incite someone to do something means to encourage or persuade them to do it, often in a way that is negative or harmful.

words.ex: The boy showed defiance by refusing to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 男孩通过拒绝遵守规则来表现违抗。
words.en: Defiance is behaviour or an attitude which shows that you are not willing to obey someone or something.

words.tr:
n. 鞭子
v. 鞭打；抽打；突然移动
words.ex: The farmer used a whip to guide the horse.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用鞭子赶马。
words.en: To whip means to hit a person or animal with a whip, or to move something quickly and suddenly.

words.tr: phrase. （通过严厉训练或管教）使变得有条理、有效率或合乎标准；整顿好
words.ex: He will whip the team into shape before the big game.
words.ex_cn: 他将在大赛前把团队训练得井井有条。
words.en: To make something or someone more organized, efficient, or effective, often by using strict methods.

words.ex: They cooperate to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他们合作以按时完成项目。
words.en: If you cooperate with someone, you work with them or help them for a particular purpose.

words.tr: adj. 典型的；有代表性的；
words.ex: This is a typical example of a sunny day.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个晴天的典型例子。
words.en: You use typical to describe someone or something that shows the most usual characteristics of a particular type of person or thing, and is therefore a good example of that type.

words.ex: The movie was fairly interesting.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影相当地有趣。
words.en: To a moderately sufficient extent or degree.

words.ex: Everyone passed the test, with one exception.
words.ex_cn: 所有人都通过了考试，只有一个例外。
words.en: An exception is a person or thing that is excluded from a general statement or does not follow a rule.

words.tr:
n. 补锅匠
v. 小修；小补；摆弄
words.ex: He is a tinker who fixes old pots and pans.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名补锅匠，修理旧锅旧盆。
words.en: If you tinker with something, you make some small changes to it in an attempt to improve it or repair it.

words.ex: He is grappled with the math problem for hours.
words.ex_cn: 他花了好几个小时努力解决这道数学题。
words.en: To grapple with something means to try hard to understand or deal with a difficult problem or subject.

words.ex: We must eliminate the waste to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须消除浪费以保护环境。
words.en: To eliminate something, especially something you do not want or need, means to remove it completely.

words.ex: A bug crawled on the leaf.
words.ex_cn: 一只小虫子爬在叶子上。
words.en: A bug is a small insect, or it can refer to a fault in a computer program or system.

words.ex: He studies dynamics to understand how forces move objects.
words.ex_cn: 他学习动态学以理解力如何使物体运动。
words.en: Dynamics is the branch of mechanics that deals with the motion of bodies under the action of forces, considering the mass and velocity of the bodies.

words.tr:
n. 吸引力；上诉；
v. 吸引；诉请；呼吁；
words.ex: The appeal of the beach drew many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 海滩的吸引力吸引了许多游客。
words.en: If you appeal to someone to do something, you make a serious and urgent request to them. If you appeal against a decision or sentence, you formally ask a court or other authority to change it. If something appeals to you, you like it or it interests you.

words.tr: phrase. 作为兼职；另外；暗地里
words.ex: He works as a teacher and drives a taxi on the side.
words.ex_cn: 他当老师，同时兼职开出租车。
words.en: If someone does something on the side, they do it in addition to their main job.

words.tr: phrase. 在顶部；在上侧；在顶面
words.ex: The bird sat on the top side of the fence.
words.ex_cn: 鸟停在篱笆的顶部。
words.en: Located at the highest part or surface of something.

words.tr: phrase. phr. 处于获胜一方；站在赢家这边；成为胜利的一方
words.ex: He was on the winning side in the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中站在了胜利的一方。
words.en: Being part of the group or team that wins in a competition, contest, or conflict.

words.tr: phrase. phr. 处于失败的一方；在败方；失利的一方
words.ex: He was on the losing side in the election.
words.ex_cn: 他在选举中站在失败的一方。
words.en: Being part of the group that does not win in a competition or conflict.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必定的；
words.ex: It is inevitable that the sun will rise tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳明天一定会升起。
words.en: If something is inevitable, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.ex: He won the spelling contest.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了拼写比赛。
words.en: A contest is a competition or a struggle for victory between individuals or groups.

words.ex: He works in a technical department.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个技术部门工作。
words.en: Technical means involving the sorts of machines, processes, and materials that are used in industry, transport, and communications.

words.tr: n. 通晓数国语言的人；语言学家；
words.ex: He is a linguist who speaks five languages.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位通晓五种语言的人。
words.en: A linguist is someone who studies language or languages, especially a person who studies linguistics.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 被……淹没；收到大量……
words.ex: The school is flooded with applications this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年学校收到了大量的申请。
words.en: To be filled or overwhelmed with a large quantity of something.

words.ex: He staggered home after drinking too much.
words.ex_cn: 他喝多了后摇摇晃晃地走回家。
words.en: If you stagger, you walk very unsteadily, as if you are about to fall.

words.ex: His generosity helped the poor family.
words.ex_cn: 他的慷慨帮助了那个贫困的家庭。
words.en: Generosity is the quality of being kind and generous.

words.tr: n. 专门知识；专门技能；
words.ex: His expertise in computers helps the team solve problems.
words.ex_cn: 他在计算机方面的专门知识帮助团队解决问题。
words.en: Expertise is special skill or knowledge that is acquired by training, study, or practice.

words.tr: n. 代码；编码；行为准则；密码；法典；
words.ex: He wrote a simple code to solve the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一段简单的代码来解决这个数学问题。
words.en: A code is a system of words, letters, figures, or other symbols substituted for other words, letters, etc., especially for the purposes of secrecy. As a verb, it means to convert (a message or other information) into a code.

words.tr:
adj. 男性的；雄性的；
n. 男性；雄性；
words.ex: The male bird has bright red feathers.
words.ex_cn: 这只雄鸟有鲜艳的红色羽毛。
words.en: A male is a person or animal that belongs to the sex that cannot have babies. In humans, males are usually considered to be boys or men.

words.ex: He explained the rules specifically.
words.ex_cn: 他具体地解释了规则。
words.en: You use specifically to emphasize that something is given special attention and considered separately from other things of the same kind.

words.tr: 短语动词。获得发言权；站起来讲话（尤指在会议或辩论中）
words.ex: He wants to get the floor to speak.
words.ex_cn: 他想发言。
words.en: To be given the opportunity to speak in a discussion or meeting.

words.tr: 短语动词，有发言权；正在发言
words.ex: Now you have the floor, please speak clearly.
words.ex_cn: 现在你有发言权，请清楚地讲话。
words.en: to have the right or opportunity to speak in a public discussion or meeting

words.ex: He uses a fake name for anonymity.
words.ex_cn: 他用假名来保持匿名。
words.en: The condition of being anonymous; the state of not having one's name or identity known.

words.tr: adj. 充满辱骂的；责骂的
words.ex: His vituperative remarks were uncalled for.
words.ex_cn: 他那些责骂的话是多余的。
words.en: If you describe something that is said or written as vituperative, you mean that it is full of bitter criticism or anger.

words.ex: I can't tolerate loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 我无法容忍巨大的噪音。
words.en: If you tolerate a situation or person, you accept them although you do not particularly like them.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人失去兴趣；使某人反感；使某人厌烦
words.ex: His constant boasting really turns me off.
words.ex_cn: 他不断的吹嘘真的让我感到厌烦。
words.en: To cause someone to lose interest or enthusiasm.

words.tr:
n. 大洪水；暴雨；泛滥
v. 泛滥；大量涌入
words.ex: The rain caused a deluge in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这场雨在镇上引发了洪水。
words.en: A deluge is a severe flood or a very heavy fall of rain that causes a lot of damage.

words.ex: The defense presented counterevidence to challenge the prosecution's claims.
words.ex_cn: 辩护方提出了反证来质疑检方的说法。
words.en: Evidence that contradicts or opposes other evidence.

words.ex: They have good rapport with their students.
words.ex_cn: 他们与学生关系友好。
words.en: A friendly relationship in which people understand each other very well.

words.ex: He conveyed his thanks with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着表达了谢意。
words.en: If you convey information or a message, you communicate it to someone, often in a way that is not direct.

words.ex: He will submit his homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会提交他的作业。
words.en: To yield or surrender (oneself) to the will or authority of another.

words.tr:
v. 衰落；减弱；缺；亏
n. 衰退；减弱；缺；亏
words.ex: The moon begins to wane after the full moon.
words.ex_cn: 满月之后，月亮开始变暗。
words.en: If something wanes, it becomes gradually weaker or less, often so that it eventually disappears.

words.ex: He added the bibliography at the end of his report.
words.ex_cn: 他在报告末尾添加了参考书目。
words.en: A bibliography is a list of the books and articles that have been used by someone when writing a particular book or article.

words.tr:
n. 平衡；天平；秤；
v. （使）相抵；（使）平衡；
words.ex: She maintains a good balance between work and rest.
words.ex_cn: 她在工作和休息之间保持良好的平衡。
words.en: Balance is the ability to remain steady when you are standing up. Also, it refers to the state of having your weight spread equally so that you do not fall. In finance, it refers to the amount of money you have in a bank account.

words.ex: He wrote a check from his checkbook.
words.ex_cn: 他从支票簿里开了一张支票。
words.en: A checkbook is a book of checks which your bank gives you so that you can pay for things by check.

words.tr: v. 嫉妒；羡慕；不乐意地做（或付出）
words.ex: He begrudges his friend's success.
words.ex_cn: 他嫉妒朋友的成功。
words.en: If you begrudge something, you feel unhappy or resentful about having to give it, do it, or allow it.

words.tr:
n. 救援；营救；
v. 救援；营救；
words.ex: The rescue came just in time to save the hikers.
words.ex_cn: 救援及时赶到，救出了徒步者。
words.en: To rescue someone or something means to save them from a dangerous or unpleasant situation.

words.tr: phrase. 处于困境中；需要帮助（或救济）的
words.ex: He is in need of help.
words.ex_cn: 他需要帮助。
words.en: If someone is in need, they are very poor and require help.

words.tr: phrase. 拜访；要求；呼吁；号召
words.ex: I will call upon my grandmother this weekend.
words.ex_cn: 这个周末我会去拜访我的祖母。
words.en: To call upon someone is to ask them to do something or to use something that they can offer.

words.ex: The knight saved the damsel from the dragon.
words.ex_cn: 骑士从龙手中救出了少女。
words.en: A damsel is a young, unmarried woman, often portrayed as being in need of rescue or protection.

words.tr: n. 流氓；无赖；小丑；（纸牌中的） J
words.ex: He was known as a cunning knave who would cheat anyone.
words.ex_cn: 他以狡猾的无赖著称，会欺骗任何人。
words.en: A man who behaves dishonestly or unscrupulously.

words.ex: I would rather stay home than go out in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 我宁愿待在家里也不愿在雨中出去。
words.en: If you say that you would rather do something or you'd rather do it, you mean that you would prefer to do it. If you say that you would rather not do something, you mean that you do not want to do it.

words.tr: phrase. 宁愿……也不……（用于表达偏好或选择）
words.ex: I would rather walk than take the bus.
words.ex_cn: 我宁愿走路也不愿坐公交车。
words.en: If you say that you would rather do something or you'd rather do it, you mean that you would prefer to do it. If you say that you would rather not do something, you mean that you do not want to do it.

words.ex: He read the booklet about the new rules.
words.ex_cn: 他读了那本关于新规则的小册子。
words.en: A booklet is a small, thin book that has a paper cover and that gives you information about something.

words.ex: The computer's hard drive is full.
words.ex_cn: 电脑的硬盘已满。
words.en: A hard drive is a piece of hardware in a computer that stores and retrieves digital information using rapidly rotating disks coated with magnetic material.

words.ex: He wields his knowledge to solve problems.
words.ex_cn: 他运用自己的知识来解决问题。
words.en: To wield something means to hold and use it, especially as a weapon or tool. It can also mean to have and be able to use power or influence.

words.tr: n. 螺丝刀；改锥；螺丝起子；伏特加橙汁鸡尾酒
words.ex: He used a screwdriver to tighten the loose screws.
words.ex_cn: 他用螺丝刀拧紧了松动的螺丝。
words.en: A screwdriver is a tool that is used for turning screws. It has a handle and a long metal part that fits into the top of the screw.

words.tr: phrase. 设法做成某事；成功完成某事
words.ex: He manages to do his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都能设法完成作业。
words.en: To succeed in doing something, especially something that requires effort or skill.
